info.title: orchestra dashboard API
info.summary: HTTP API over a running orchestra backend: reads everything it knows, and changes what it is configured with.
info.description:
Everything the daemon knows about its queue, task history, listeners, projects and authentication sources, as JSON. Every read is also available as a Server-Sent Events stream at the same path under `/sse/v1/`, pushed every two seconds and only when the payload has changed.

Three resources are configuration and are writable: **listeners**, **roles** and **skills**. Everything else — the queue, task history, concerts, projects, authentication sources — is a record of something that already happened or is owned by another system, and is read-only here. Nothing in this API enqueues or cancels work; that is the daemon's control socket.

## Writing

- Every route that is not a `GET` requires a credential. `POST /api/login` is the only exception, since it is how one is obtained.
- Every write must be sent as `application/json`. A request without that content type is a `415`. This is the second of the two locks on a cookie-authenticated write: the session cookie is `SameSite=Strict`, so a cross-site request carries no credential, and an HTML form cannot send JSON, so it cannot form the request at all.
- `POST` to a collection creates and refuses to overwrite (`409`), taking the name from the body. `PUT` to a member creates or replaces, taking the name from the path; a body naming a different one is a `400`.
- `DELETE` answers `204`, or `404` when there was nothing there.
- A rejected body changes nothing on disk: validation runs to completion before anything is written, and every write is a write-and-rename, so a reader never sees a partial file.
- Listener configs and roles are stored **verbatim**, not re-serialised. That is what keeps `{{secret}}` placeholders — and any field a client does not know about — intact across an edit. Fetch the `config` field of a detail response, change it, and `PUT` it back.

## Conventions

- Instants are RFC 3339 in UTC (`2026-07-23T10:04:11Z`) and live in a field named `...At`.
- Durations are integer seconds, in a field named `...Seconds`.
- An absent value is `null`, never an empty string.
- Enumerations are the lower-case names the daemon itself uses.
- Collections answer in a common envelope (`items`, `total`, `limit`, `offset`) and accept `limit`, `offset` and — where the collection is ordered by time — `since`.
- A parameter that is malformed, or that the collection cannot honour, is a `400`. Parameters this version does not define are ignored.

get.description: Served without a credential and outside the version prefix: a client has to be able to discover what it is talking to before it can authenticate. Always the spec of the binary answering, not of a checkout.

200.description: The OpenAPI description of this API.

get.summary: Whether the caller holds a valid credential
get.description: Reachable without one, deliberately: it is what a client asks on load to decide between logging in and proceeding, and it discloses nothing that trying any other endpoint would not.

post.summary: Exchange the password for a session cookie
post.description: For browsers. A script should send `Authorization: Bearer <password>` on each request instead and never call this.

200.description: Accepted. The session id comes back in an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict` cookie.

post.description: Reachable without a credential, like `POST /api/login`: revoking a session one may no longer hold is not a privileged act, and requiring a valid one would mean an expired session could not be cleared.

200.description: Revoked, and the cookie cleared. Sessions live in memory, so a restart revokes every session anyway.

get.summary: One-request summary of the whole daemon
get.description: An aggregate, not a resource: counts plus two short projections, so a dashboard can render a first screen — and keep it current over one SSE stream — without fanning out. Everything in it is available in full from the collections below. It takes no parameters; the projections are deliberately fixed in size.
Work waiting or running, newest first. Includes entries in terminal states that have not yet been cleared.

get.summary: One task, with the tail of its log
get.description: Resolves against task history first and the queue second, so a run that is still in flight is addressable by the same id.

parameters.name: logLimit
parameters.description: How many trailing log events to return.

get.description: Multi-step workflow runs, newest first. Ordered and filtered by `startedAt`.

get.summary: One concert run and its steps

get.description: Configuration rather than events, so this collection has no time order and does not accept `since`.

post.description:
The body is the listener config document itself — exactly what is stored at `<config>/listeners/<name>.json` — and the name comes from its `name` field. Refuses to overwrite; `PUT /api/v1/listeners/{name}` replaces.

The daemon re-reads listener configs on every tick and rescans the directory every fifteen seconds, so a listener created here starts polling without a restart.

get.summary: One listener, with its source and the task it enqueues

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Listener name. Percent-encode it; a component that could name a path is rejected as not found.

put.description: The body is the listener config document itself. Its `name` must equal the path component — a mismatch is a `400` rather than a silent rename, because the two spellings would otherwise disagree for as long as the file exists.

delete.description:
Removes the config and the state that belonged to it. The state is a list of event ids already handled, and keeping it would mean a listener re-created under the same name silently ignored every event its predecessor had seen.

The daemon's fiber for this listener retires within one tick of its config disappearing.

put.summary: Turn a listener on or off
put.description: A sub-resource rather than a field of the config, because `enabled` lives in the listener's *state* file: turning one off is an operational act and must not require — or risk — rewriting its configuration. Takes effect on the listener's next tick.

get.description:
The roles in `<config>/roles/`. A project may shadow one by name under its own directory; that copy belongs to the project and is not served or written here.

Configuration rather than events, so this collection has no time order and does not accept `since`.

200.description: A page of roles, ordered by name.

post.description:
The body is the role document itself, and the name comes from its `name` field. Refuses to overwrite.

`permissions` is checked against the tool groups the sandbox actually grants (`create_pr`, `comment`, `label_issue`, `manage_issues`, `work_issues`, `review_issues`); a typo there is otherwise invisible until a dispatched agent finds itself without the tool it was told to use.

get.summary: One role, with its prompt template and the document behind it
get.description: A role file that exists but does not parse still answers, with `parseError` set and the derived fields absent — the point of a configuration API is to show the operator the file that needs fixing, not a `404` for something plainly there.

put.description: The body is the role document itself; its `name` must equal the path component. Takes effect on the dispatcher's next tick — roles are read per dispatch, not cached.

delete.description: A project-scoped role of the same name is left alone: it shadows the global one rather than extending it, so removing the global file does not remove the role from that project.

get.description: The Markdown documents under `<config>/skills/skills/`, which every agent this instance launches is handed. Ordered by name.

post.description: A skill is Markdown, which a JSON body cannot be, so it travels wrapped: `{"name": "…", "content": "---\nname: …"}`. Refuses to overwrite.

put.description:
The `content` must open with a YAML front matter block carrying a `name` matching the path component and a non-empty `description`. Both are required rather than optional: an agent reads the description to decide whether a skill is relevant before it reads the body, so a file without one is loaded and then never used.

Takes effect for tasks launched after the write. A task already running keeps the skills it started with.

delete.description: Removes the whole skill directory, which is the unit the plugin layout defines: a skill's supporting files live beside its `SKILL.md`, and leaving them behind would leave something that is not a skill and not nothing.

get.description: Configuration rather than events, so this collection does not accept `since`.

500.description: The tracker could not be reached. The body carries what went wrong.

get.summary: One project and its issue dependency graph

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Taxis project id. An id that is not an integer is not found rather than looked up.

get.summary: Configured authentication sources and their usage limits
get.description:
Read from the usage store the daemon maintains, never polled live: the upstream endpoint meters requests, so a client that polled it every couple of seconds would rate-limit the very thing it is monitoring. `polledAt` on each source is how fresh the numbers are.

Open this when the queue has pending work and nothing is running.

bearerAuth.description: The dashboard password, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <password>`. This is the path for scripts. The password comes from `--password`, `$ORCHESTRA_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD`, or `<data>/dashboard.secret`.

sessionCookie.name: orchestra_session
sessionCookie.description: Issued by `POST /api/login`. `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Strict`, so it also authenticates `EventSource` connections without putting a credential in a URL.

limit.name: limit
limit.description: Maximum items to return. Values above the maximum are clamped to it rather than rejected.

offset.name: offset
offset.description: Items to skip. Compare against `total`, which counts matches before the window.

since.name: since
since.description: Keep only items at or after this instant. Accepted only by collections ordered by time.

name.name: name
name.description: Configuration record name. Percent-encode it; a component that could name a path is rejected as not found.

id.name: id
id.description: Resource id. Percent-encode it; a component that could name a path is rejected as not found.

BadRequest.description: A parameter was malformed, or is not one this endpoint accepts.

Unauthorized.description: No credential, or one that is not valid.

Conflict.description: A record of that name already exists. `POST` never overwrites; `PUT` does.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The write did not declare `application/json`. A deliberate lock, not a parser limitation — see the write conventions above.

Deleted.description: Deleted. No body, because there is nothing left to describe.

ListenerWritten.description: The listener as `GET /api/v1/listeners/{name}` would return it.

RoleWritten.description: The role as `GET /api/v1/roles/{name}` would return it.

SkillWritten.description: The skill as `GET /api/v1/skills/{name}` would return it.

Error.description: The body of every non-2xx response.

error.description: What went wrong, in one sentence.

Collection.description: The envelope every collection answers in.

limit.description: The window size actually used, after clamping.

QueueEntry.description: Work waiting or running. Becomes a Task when it is claimed; `taskId` is that run.

taskId.description: The run this entry became, once claimed.

continuesFrom.description: Id of the run this one resumed.

log.description: The trailing `logLimit` events of the run's structured log, oldest first. Event shape is the agent backend's, not this API's, and is deliberately not constrained here.

logTotal.description: Events in the log in total.

logTruncated.description: Whether `log` is a tail rather than the whole.

ListenerConfig.description: A listener config document, exactly as stored at `<config>/listeners/<name>.json`. Stored verbatim rather than re-serialised, so `{{secret}}` placeholders and fields this version does not model both survive an edit; it is validated after secret substitution, which is how the daemon reads it. The `source` union and the `action` template are documented in the repository README under "Listeners".

name.description: Must equal the name it is stored under.

source.description: What to watch. `type` selects the variant: `github-issues`, `github-pr-reviews`, `github-comments`, `github-labels`, `github-label-count`, `shell`, `project-dispatcher`, `label-dispatcher`.

action.description: The task to enqueue when it fires. `mode` and `prompt_template` are required.

interval_seconds.description: Poll interval. Zero is rejected: a listener polling zero seconds apart would spin against its source as fast as the network allows.

RoleConfig.description: A role document, exactly as stored at `<config>/roles/<name>.json`. Stored verbatim.

name.description: Must equal the name it is stored under.

permissions.description: Optional tool groups the agent is granted. The always-available tools are not listed here; naming them grants nothing.

prompt_template.description: The prompt body. Must not be empty — a role with nothing to say dispatches an agent with an empty prompt.

DispatchPolicy.description: When the dispatcher may spawn this role automatically. Absent (`null`) means manual-spawn only.

max.description: Default cap when a dispatcher config omits one. `0` means auto-spawn is opt-in.

preClaim.description: For `has_open_issues` roles: claim the issue at spawn time.

Role.description: A global role, as the API renders it.

parseError.description: Set when the file exists but is not a role. The derived fields above are then absent and only `name` and `config` are meaningful.

config.description: The document as stored. This is what to edit and `PUT` back.

Skill.description: One skill: a Markdown document handed to every agent this instance launches.

name.description: Directory name under `skills/`, and the front matter's `name`.

description.description: The front matter's `description`. `null` only for a file put there by hand without one.

SkillWrite.description: A skill on the way in. Markdown cannot be a JSON body, so it travels wrapped.

name.description: Required by `POST`, which names the skill from the body; ignored by `PUT`, which names it from the path.

content.description: The whole `SKILL.md`. Must open with a `---` front matter block carrying a `name` matching the path and a non-empty `description`.

recentEvents.description: Ids of the most recently processed events, newest first.

config.description: The document as stored, `{{secret}}` placeholders unexpanded. Everything above it is derived and is what a display wants; this is what to edit and `PUT` back. `null` when the file could not be read.

ListenerAction.description: The task a listener enqueues when its source matches.

workflowPath.description: Set when the listener enqueues a whole concert.

id.description: Taxis id, as a string so it can be compared and put in a URL without numeric coercion.

Issue.description: One node of a project's dependency graph.

dependencies.description: Issue ids that must finish first.

scope.description: Model family a scoped limit applies to.

active.description: Whether this limit is currently the binding one.

backend.description: Agent backend this source belongs to.

isDefault.description: What a task that names no source gets.

pollable.description: False for API-key sources, which bill per token and have no window to report.

availableAt.description: When the block lifts. `null` when available, and also when blocked with no reported reset.

pressure.description: Highest limit percentage across this source, as a fraction.

backoffUntil.description: Set only while a polling backoff is still in the future.

configError.description: Set instead of `backends` when the config could not be read.

taxisUrl.description: Base URL of the configured taxis tracker, or `null` if none is configured. Projects live in taxis and are its business to display; this is what a client links out to instead of rendering them, and `null` means there is nothing to link to.

activeQueue.description: Running and pending entries. Not paged; use `/api/v1/queue` for the full list.

recentTasks.description: The ten most recent runs. Use `/api/v1/tasks` for more.

x-sse.description:
Every path under `/api/v1/` that answers a `GET` is also a Server-Sent Events stream at the same path under `/sse/v1/`, carrying the identical JSON payload in the `data` field of each `message` event. Query parameters mean the same thing on both.

Frames are pushed every two seconds, but only when the payload has changed since the last one, so an idle daemon costs nothing; a `: keep-alive` comment goes out every thirty seconds of silence to survive idle proxies. A stream whose resource disappears, or whose parameters are rejected, is closed rather than left hanging.

Authenticate with the session cookie or the bearer header, exactly as for the JSON routes.
